cohort: Pregnant women with singleton pregnancies >= 37 weeks, who delivered between March 2020 and June 2023, excluding those with fetal malformations, chromosomal anomalies, or missing data.
finding: The presence of a nuchal cord generally had no effect on adverse perinatal outcomes, but a tight nuchal cord was associated with a 7.52-fold increased risk of an Apgar score < 7 at the 1st minute.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with a nuchal cord had a higher prevalence of cesarean sections (99% vs. 60.4%).
